Welcome to the official website of the Department of Pharmacy at the United International University (UIU). We are thrilled to announce that our Bachelor of Pharmacy (B. Pharm.) program has been approved by both the University Grants Commission (UGC) of Bangladesh and the Pharmacy Council of Bangladesh (PCB) in 2023. At our department, we are committed to delivering quality education and conducting cutting-edge research in Pharmaceutical Sciences. Our comprehensive 4-year B. Pharm. program spans 8 semesters and with a total of 160 credits. It offers a wide range of knowledge in pharmacy and related fields. To support our academic pursuits, we have fully equipped state-of-the-art laboratories, including the Inorganic and Physical Pharmacy Laboratory, Organic Pharmacy  Medicinal Chemistry Laboratory, Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry Laboratory, Pharmaceutical Analysis Laboratory, Pharmaceutical Microbiology Laboratory, and Physiology  Pharmacology Laboratory. Our B. Pharm. program aims to produce highly skilled pharmacy graduates capable of excelling in all aspects of pharmaceutical services. As part of the program, students undergo three months of non-credit training in hospitals upon completion of the course and one-month in-plant training in the pharmaceutical industry. These experiences aim to cultivate competitive professionals who can thrive nationally and internationally. Our B. Pharm. program opens up diverse opportunities for graduates in various sectors of the healthcare system, including industrial pharmacy, pharmaceutical marketing, hospital pharmacy, clinical pharmacy, community pharmacy, and research, among others. With the advancement of new and potent drugs, pharmacists now play a crucial role in providing patients with accurate medication information while ensuring drug safety and efficacy. As the Head of the Department, I take great pride in the rigorous curriculum we offer, the excellent laboratory facilities we provide, and our team of highly qualified faculty members. Our faculty members have obtained their degrees from prestigious institutions at home and abroad. Their expertise enables us to produce well-qualified and skilled pharmacists who can serve the pharmaceutical sector domestically and internationally and other government sectors related to health and research. Thank you for visiting our website. We hope it will provide you all the necessary information you need. If you have any further inquiries, please feel free to contact us. Dr. Tahmina FoyezAssociate Professor  Head,Department of PharmacySchool of Life Sciences

Following entry requirements will be considered for the students seeking admission to pursue the Bachelor of Pharmacy (B.Pharm.) program in the Department of Pharmacy at United International University. 01. SSC and HSC Result: Candidates are required to have a minimum aggregate GPA of 8.00 (out of 10) in SSCEquivalent and HSCEquivalent examinations. Specifically, they must achieve a minimum GPA of 3.50 (out of 5) in the Science group in both examinations. 02. In SSCEquivalent examination: Candidates must achieve a minimum GPA of 4.00 in Chemistry and Biology and 3.50 in Physics and Mathematics. 03. In HSCEquivalent examination: Candidates must achieve a minimum GPA of 4.00 in Chemistry and Biology and 3.50 in Physics and Mathematics. However, candidates without Mathematicshaving GPA below 3.5 in HSC recognized equivalent examination can be admitted but need to take an additional 3- credit course in Mathematics during B. pharm. study. 04. HSC Passing year: Candidates must have passed the HSC recognized equivalent examination in the current year or the preceding year. For example, candidates applying for the Spring 2024 semester must have passed their HSCrecognized equivalent examination in 2022 or 2023. 05.O Level and A Level Candidates: Candidates with O-level and A-level must have a minimum grade of B in Chemistry and Biology, and a minimum grade of C in Physics and Mathematics in both exams. Candidates without Mathematics need to take an additional 3 credit course in Mathematics during B. pharm study. They are not required to obtain an equivalence certificate from the Pharmacy Council before application for admission. 06. Foreign Students: Foreign students must have completed 12 years of education and obtained equivalent grades in examinations recognized by relevant foreign institutions. They are required to obtain an equivalence certificate from the Pharmacy Council before application for admission. 07. Acceptable score in UIU Admission Test. Note: Students who pass the written admission test may need to have viva voce (oral interview) as part of the admission selection process.

title: Syed Masudur Rahman Dewan - UIU - Department of Pharmacy
content: Dr. Syed Masudur Rahman Dewan Assistant Professor, Department of Pharmacy ROOM: 835 (A) PABX: 7211 Email: masudurpharmacy.uiu.ac.bd Biography Dr. Dewan earned his Ph.D. in Medical Sciences from Tokyo Medical and Dental University (TMDU), Japan in 2021 with a scholarship from the Japanese Government (MEXT: Monbukagakusho). His doctoral studies include the elucidation of the mechanistic progression of acute vascular inflammation by qualitative changes through the interaction between neutrophils and the endothelium induced by the complement protein C5a. He also focused on the induction of chronic inflammation by complement-stimulated neutrophil-induced monocyte migration in the context of atherosclerosis. Presently, he is engaged in research concerning the correlation between susceptible gene polymorphisms in cardiovascular diseases and cancer risks among the Bangladeshi populace. Additionally, he collaborates in several studies that examine various concurrent public health concerns. Dr. Dewan graduated from Noakhali Science and Technology University (NSTU) in 2011 with a major in Pharmacy, subsequently earning an M.Pharm in Clinical Pharmacy and Pharmacology from the same institution in 2013. Throughout his undergraduate and postgraduate studies, his research primarily focused on conducting case-control studies on prehepatic jaundice, preeclampsia, and schizophrenia. These studies investigated the correlation between socio-economic conditions and levels of lipid peroxidation, enzymatic or non-enzymatic antioxidants, as well as alterations in trace element levels, exploring their implications in disease etiology. Additionally, Dr. Dewan contributed to various projects examining the pharmacological effectssuch as antipyretic, analgesic, anthelmintic, antimicrobial, antioxidant, and thrombolytic effectsof numerous medicinal plants indigenous to Bangladesh, both in vitro and in vivo. After completing his undergraduate studies, he served as a Production Officer at ACI Limited for approximately two years, overseeing the manufacturing of cephalosporin drugs. Following the completion of his PhD, Dr. Dewan commenced his academic career as a Lecturer at Dhaka International University, subsequently joining the University of Asia Pacific (UAP) as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Pharmacy. Dr. Dewan holds honorary memberships in prestigious organizations including the Japan Atherosclerosis Society, the Japan Cardiovascular Association, and the European Society of Cardiology. He serves on the editorial boards of distinguished journals such as Scientific Reports (Nature Publishing Group) and the Journal of Food Biochemistry (Wiley). Additionally, he is recognized as a prominent reviewer for numerous esteemed national and international scientific journals. His research interests encompass vascular biology, inflammation, genetic polymorphism, pharmacology, and public health. title: Notice Regarding Resumption of Academic Activities - United International University (UIU)
content: Notice Notice Regarding Resumption of Academic Activities Publish Date : August 27, 2024 As we all are aware, the academic activities of the United International University (UIU) remained suspended since July 16, 2024. Just as the students of other educational institutions throughout Bangladesh, the courageous students of UIU have also joined the Quota ReformAnti-Discrimination Movement with determination to ensure their right. We lost Shaheed Md. Irfan Bhuiyan; and scores others got injured and suffered detention. Finally, our students came out victorious. UIU is proud of its students. When we planned to resume our academic activities from August 24, 2024 online, another disaster struck the South-Eastern part of Bangladesh. Our students again stood by the helpless flood-affected people. Many of our students are still working in the flood-affected areas serving the humanity. Despite all this, UIU needs to resume its academic activities in the educational interest of our students. We have already lost one-and-a-half months from our academic life. In order to bring our students back to their academic activities, and in reference to our notice of August 17, 2024, we have decided the followings: On-campus classes of all studentstrimester, semester, post-graduate, etc.will be held from September 01, 2024 (Sunday); A dua mahfil will be organised, in memory of Shaheed Md. Irfan Bhuiyan, on September 01, 2024 at the Masjid Al-Mustafa at 11:30 AM with the attendance of all from the UIU family (students, faculty, admin, etc.); Inauguration of the Shaheed Irfan Library (UIU Library), the Swadhinata Corner in the library, and the Irfan Maintenance Lab will be held on September 01, 2024; A cheque of Tk. 50,00,000 (Take Fifty Lakhs) will be handed over to the father of Shaheed Md. Irfan Bhuiyan on September 01, 2024; There will be no class testquiz in the first week of September 2024 (01 to 06 September); Special academic arrangements (missed classes counselling; taking of missed CTAssignment at suitable time, etc.) will be made for the students, who will join us later after their services in the flood-affected areas are completed, or who are severely affected by floods; and Considering the overall situation of our students, who are faced with different types of difficulties, the last date for Trimester Drop for Summer 2024 is extended up to September 15, 2024 with full refund. UIU is eagerly waiting to welcome our students back to their campus on September 01, 2024. Dr. Md. Zulfiqur Rahman Registrar NOTICES October 8, 2025 Expulsion of Md. title: UIU Social Services Club Stands beside the Remal Affected People in Khulna - United International University (UIU)
content: News UIU Social Services Club Stands beside the Remal Affected People in Khulna June 25, 2024 SHARE: UIU Social Services Club (UIU SSSC), a wing of the Directorate of Career Counseling and Student Affairs (DCCSA) of United International University (UIU), recently collected an emergency fund to extend a hand of supports to the distressed families in Remal cyclone affected areas at Koyra in Khulna. In this area, hundreds of people have been severely affected by the recent devastating cyclone and became homeless and lost farms. The young members of UIU Social Services Club raised a fund for the cyclone-affected people. They collected donations from the faculties, officers and students of UIU and properly distributed the collected amount among 50 cyclone affected families for the assistance of their rehabilitation. This finance may help them to suppress their hardship and recover from their situation, even for a little bit. Renata PLC was the Health Care Partner and Bonik Barta and the Daily Campus were the media partners. A team consisting of seven members of the Social Services Club marched on Thursday, 13 June 2024 to the remote insuperable area at Koyra and collected data. They sorted out and selected the exact people who were actually affected and severely jeopardized. As a part of the social responsibility, the UIU Social Services Club is committed to serving the community from the bottom of their hearts. Mr. Mifthahur Rahman Himel, President of UIU Social Services Club, said that We are always prepared to support the people during such calamities. we must stand by them with whatever resources we have. Professor Dr. Md. Abul Kashem Mia Vice Chancellor of UIU thanks to all the faculty members, administrative officers and students who stood beside the Remal-affected people. He also expressed his gratitude to everyone involved in making the campaign a success especially Prof. Dr. A.K.M. Mujahidul Islam, Director of DCCSA and Dr. Abdullah Al Mamun, Moderator of UIUSSC for their proactive coordination. title: Message from The Head - UIU- Department of English
content: Message from The Head AboutMessage from The Head Why Choose B.A. in English at UIU? NoticesJuly 15, 2025Course Registration of the Summer 2025 Trimester for the Newly Admitted Students and Current Students of the Department English.June 30, 2025Course Final Advising Summer 2025 TrimesterFebruary 16, 2025Notice: Course Advising and Registration for Spring-2025 TrimesterDecember 21, 2024Course EvaluationOctober 19, 2024Reschedule of Mid-term ExaminationView moreNewsAugust 14, 2024Et ut proident, tene.View moreEventsAugust 15, 2024 12:00 amExcepteur officia si.View more Welcome to the Department of English The Department of English at United International University was launched on the 12th of December, 2023, and the English Language Institute (ELI) was merged with the Department of English on the mentioned date. Prior to the launching of the Department of English, the English Language Institute (ELI) began its journey along with the inception of United International University in 2003. The primary objective of ELI was to analyse English as a Second Language (ESL)English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners language needs and facilitate them accordingly by designing and updating the courses. At present, the Department of English offers two major streams; one concentration is on Applied Linguistics and ELT, and the other one is on Literature. Along with core English Courses, the Department of English also offers two non-departmental fundamental courses, namely English I and English II, and both of the courses are compulsory for the new entrants of the School of Business and Economics and School of Science and Engineering and other departments. The B.A. in English programme at UIU is designed to provide a broad spectrum of English studies, i.e. literary genres, critical theories, applied linguistics and theories of ELT, niche in research orientation, and hands-on teaching experience. The programme will mould students to pursue interdisciplinary courses that are expected to broaden their outlook and develop their liberal and humane values. Our B.A. programme encompasses a wide range of topics, from traditional subjects like Romanticism, Shakespeare, world literature, and composition techniques to more modern subjects like advanced critical theories, ecocriticism, cultural studies, migration literature, and English as a secondforeign language (ESLEFL) in light of current developments in the teaching and learning of foreign languages. At the bachelors level, students can opt for a degree to specialize in either literature or ELT and applied linguistics, and there are substantial resources, cooperation and collaboration available to help them carry out their research work independently. As a result, our curricula are tailored to give students the tools they need to explore the world both inside and outside of the classroom and to be ready to face the challenges of the twenty-first century. The faculty members of the Department of English have noteworthy research publications. Hopefully, our passing-out graduates will teach at reputable universities both at home and abroad, as well as in the corporate sector, media, civil service, and many other fields. They will teach at colleges and high schools, work in humanities centres, and be employed by non-profit organizations, the private sector, and the public sector. Their research and teaching efforts will help to shape the corpus of current knowledge. The major links on the website will provide you with information on the departments history, admissions practices, and faculty profiles; the quick links will take you to announcements, departmental publications, and newsletters alerting you to the flurry of activities occurring here. When in need, dont be afraid to get in touch with our energetic teachers and committed office personnel. Allow this department to provide a solid foundation for you as you grow as a person and a student. Welcome to your very own little universe of ideas, messages, excitement, and cooperation! With regards Dr. Md. Kamrul HasanAssociate Professor  HeadDepartment of EnglishUnited International University

Without any exception, every applicant who intends to pursue B.A. in English at United International University (henceforth UIU) must fulfil the admission requirements as laid down by UIU. A higher secondary certificate or its equivalent in science, arts, commerce, or other fields of study is the basic educational requirement. The related requirements for getting admitted into this programme are in the following: Candidates having a minimum GPA of 2.52nd divisionequivalent grade in SSC and HSC or equivalent public examinations are eligible to apply for getting admitted into this programme. Students with GPA 2.00 in any examination either SSC or HSC; however, they must have a minimum GPA of 6.00 totalling the GPA of both the examinations. O-level students must have completed a minimum of 5 subjects with Average Grade Point of 2.50 or above and A-level students a minimum of 2 subjects with Average Grade Point of 2.00 or above (scale A5, B4, C3, D2, E1) The students, who are sonsdaughters of freedom fighters, will be eligible for getting admission if they have a minimum GPA of 5.00 totalling the GPA of S.S.C. and H.S.C. examinations. Such students, however, have to submit the copy of authenticated certificate as the proof of hisher fathermothers identity as a freedom fighter. However, applicants will be evaluated on the basis of both previous academic achievement and UIU admission test score. Candidates must have acceptable score in UIU admission test. Moreover, a student whose IELTS band score (academic) is 6.0 or equivalent Score in Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) not less than 550 in the TOEFL Paper Based Test or80 in the TOEFL Internet Based Test or its equivalent band score might be exempted from taking UIU admission test (written and oral). Categorically, all the students must appear before a personal interview as a part of the admission requirements. Admission test is not required for GPA 5.00 holders in H.S.C.equivalent level of exams and credit transferred students for getting admission to an undergraduate program. Course WaiverTransfer Policy A student must have obtained at least a grade of B or equivalent in a similar course from any prestigious universityinstitution for course waivertransfer. A student may be allowed maximum course waiver up to 60 credit hours (20 courses) based on the recommendation of the course equivalence committee.

content: Welcome Message AboutWelcome Message Why MSJ at UIU? The present era is significantly marked with the rise of diverse media which continuously impacts dynamics of human communication. We are experiencing that the traditional mainstream news media are being shifted to the newly emerged digital and social media platforms to a larger extent. This shifting has an impact on the mass media as well as diverse organizations including the government, non-government, semi-government and autonomous. The scope of communication has extended many folds in the corporates, multinational companies, NGOs, bank and financial institutions, export-import agencies and so on. Management of digital and social media has become an indispensable part for many organizations. In order to cope with these recent transformations, demand for skilled human resources in communication and media sector is critical. Considering this demand of the day, the Department of Media Studies and Journalism (MSJ) has become one of the core areas of studies in the United International University (UIU). This department prepares you as an effective leader so that you can contribute to the formation of an equitable society enriched in human values, rights and dignity. After completion of the program, you will be skilled in the fields of communication and development, public relations (PR) and corporate communication, multimedia journalism, TV program production and anchoring, audio-visual content making, journalism and media research, and so on. Thus, you can choose the best career option that suits your dream! I am very happy to welcome to the website of our department and hope that you find the necessary information you are seeking for and many more. Dr. Sheikh Mohammad Shafiul IslamHead, MSJ-UIU

The specific objectives of the program include to: expedite the graduates conceptualize, analyze and acquire extensive knowledge of human communication, media and journalism; enable the students to become high-skilled and sensible media and communication professionals and responsible citizens of the country; enhance students ability in critical thinking, decision making and problem-solving in media, communication and journalism; cultivate managerial, entrepreneurial, and leadership skills in journalism and communication; facilitate experiential learning, research, training and advocacy in the diverse fields of human communication; develop a strong foundation in the areas of latest media and communication technologies especially in communication and media convergence driven by internet-based social media digital platforms; contribute to the societies positive transformation through advocacy for media literacy, social changes, good governance and sustainable developments.

After completing BSS (Honours) in Media Studies and Journalism (MSJ) Program, the students will become suitable professionals by learning theoretical perspectives, practical know-hows, professional ethics and human values. The human communication is an eclectic discipline which is always undergoing persistent transformation. The trend of revolution in the sector has been more visible for the technological innovations especially driven by the internet-based online communication. Such changes have created communication convergence demanding new knowledge, skills and professional competencies. Producing capable graduates for addressing the growing needs of media and communication industries in Bangladesh is critical in the present context. The academic programme has been designed in a manner which facilitates the media and communication sectors with the services of the proficient human resources. Every applicant without any exception must fulfill the admission requirements as laid down by UIU. A Higher Secondary Certificate or its equivalent in Science, Arts, Business Studies or other fields of study is the basic educational requirement. Candidates having at least GPA of 2.50 in SSC and HSC or in equivalent degrees are eligible to apply for admission to the Bachelor of Social Science (BSS) in Media Studies and Journalism Program. Candidates who have passed at least 5 papers in GCE O Level (with Mathematics as one of the subjects) and two papers of A Level may also apply provided that they have obtained 2.5 points (weighted average) in both O  A level computed according to the following scale: A5, B4, C3, D2 and E1.GED results will, however, not be accepted. Application will, however, be evaluated on the basis of the both previous academic achievements and university Admission Test scores. Admission Test will consist of a written examination on language, mathematics, general knowledge and analytical skills, followed by an interview conducted by the university.

title: Dr. Sheikh Mohammad Shafiul Islam - UIU - Media Studies and Journalism (MSJ)
content: Dr. Sheikh Mohammad Shafiul Islam Associate Professor  Head of the Department ROOM: 618 (A) PABX: 7401 Email: shafiulmsj.uiu.ac.bd, headmsj.uiu.ac.bd Summary of Professional Expertise I am Dr. Sheikh Mohammad Shafiul Islam, a senior media academic and researcher. I have been teaching Journalism, Communication and Media Studies at graduate and post graduate level since last 18 years. Apart from teaching, I have rendered consultancy services to the British Council, World Bank, Helvetas Germany, GIZ, Article19, USAID-PROGATI, HelpAge International, HomeNet South Asia, International Labour Organization (ILO), and International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), Save the Children International, Concern Worldwide, Handicap International, and International Organization for Migration (IOM). I have also served many national development organizations and institutions including the Press Institute Bangladesh (PIB), Public Administration Training Centre (PATC), National Institute of Mass Communication(NIMCO), University of Dhaka, Institute for Environment and Development (IED), Fair Election Monitoring Alliance (FEMA), Bangladesh Centre for Development, Journalism and Communication (BCDJC), Development Consultants and Global Compliance Initiatives (DCGCI), Bangla Communications Ltd. Labaid Group Ltd. I have designed and conducted more than 50 research and training projects and communication strategies. Some of my research reports have been published abroad. I have trained more than 10,000 journalists, communication professionals, government officials, human resource managers, health professionals, civil society members, researchers and development workers in home and abroad. I maintain a professional liaison with multiple stakeholders i.e. the press clubs, reporters unions, international development partners and civil society. I am frequently invited as a talk show discussant, journalists trainer and public speaker. Published BooksChapters and Research Reports 1. title: About SOBE - UIU - School of Business and Economics
content: About SOBE About SOBE The School of Business and Economics has 68 full-time faculty members, as well as a number of part-time faculty members. The school offers three undergraduate programs: Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA): The BBA program has been designed to produce graduates with the state-of-the-art knowledge, skills and understanding of the functioning of modern business enterprise. BBA program of UIU is one of top within the country and attracts a large number of students each year. Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) in Accounting  Information Systems (AIS): The BBA in AIS is an internationally recognized degree at undergraduate level that prepares potential accounting professionals, business executives, entrepreneurs and academics. The program started in 2010. UIU is the only university, which offers a full BBA program catering to the need of Accounting Professionals. Students graduating from AIS are readily capable to sit for Professional Exams (CA, ACCA, CMA, etc) of Accounting. Bachelor of Science (BS) in Economics: This program started in 2010. The program aims at providing the basic philosophy of modern economic theories with analyses on the state of contemporary economy of the world. The School of Business and Economics also offers three masters programs and one post graduate diploma program: Master of Business Administration (MBA) (Regular and Executive): The MBA program has been developed to sharpen the leadership skills in individuals who intend to pursue a management career. Specially, the program aims at making an individual thoughtful, analytic decision maker and excellent communicator. The Executive MBA program has been specially designed for executives who intend to enhance their skills further for a successful future career. Master of Science (MS) in Economics: The emphasis of the program is given in teaching applied economics courses to help graduates meeting the challenges of designing and evaluating policies. PGDHRM (Post Graduate Diploma in HRM): The PGDHRM is another exclusive program for HR professionals. UIU is again the only university among other Institutes offering this certification program in collaboration with Bangladesh Society for Human Resource Management (BSHRM).

Fouzul Kabir Khan is an economist and finance professional with a career spanning academia, government, and the private sector. He was Secretary of Power, Government of Bangladesh. He has also taught for over 15 years as a professor of Economics at North South Universitys MBA program, as a Senior Fellow at National University of Singapore, instructor at University of Massachusetts at Boston, Visiting Professor (part-time) at BRAC University and East-West University. He has lecturedoffered courses at National Defense College, Bangladesh Public Administration Training Complex, Foreign Service Academy, and for ADFIMI in Turkey, Azerbaijan, Singapore, Bali and other places. He has co-authored a book, Financing Large Projects, published by PerasonPrentice Hall, and has done extensive consulting work for the World Bank, ADB, IFC, UNDP, GtZ, and JICA in various countries. title: Universal Basic Income for All in Bangladesh: An Approach towards ensuring a Welfare State. - UIU - School of Business and Economics
content: News Universal Basic Income for All in Bangladesh: An Approach towards ensuring a Welfare State. November 27, 2024 SHARE: Ms. Tasneem Jahan Tumpa, Lecturer of Economics at United International University (UIU), participated in the dialogue on Assessing the Viability of Universal Basic Income (UBI) in Bangladesh organized by the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) with support from the European Union (EU). She represented UIUs Department of Economics in the program held at Lakeshore Hotel, Gulshan, Dhaka, on 24 November, 2024. To promote the concept of a welfare state by reducing the poverty gap and income inequality, CPD has proposed implementing a social safety net called Universal Basic Income, through which all citizens of a country may regularly receive a minimum income in cash transfers. Dr. Debapriya Bhattacharya, a renowned macroeconomist, public policy analyst and distinguished fellow at CPD, chaired the session. Professor Rehman Sobhan, a prominent economist and founder chairman of CPD, attended as a chief guest. Other distinguished panelists and stakeholders also participated in the discussion and contributed to evaluating the successful management of the UBI proposal. At the end of the session, Ms. Tasneem Jahan Tumpa exchanged views with Dr. Debapriya Bhattacharya, Professor Mustafizur Rahman, Mr. Towfiqul Islam Khan and other dignitaries who joined the session. title: Course Plan - UIU - Department of Biotechnology and Genetic Engineering
content: Course Plan UG ProgramAdmission Requirements Course Plan Curriculum Structure Program Requirement Degree Requirements Name of the Courses for the Bachelor Program in Biotechnology and Genetic Engineering General Education (GED) Courses: Basic English Course Code: ENG 1105 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course objectives: The objective of the course is to improve students overall English competency on speaking, reading, listening, and writing. Students will get an elaborate introduction to English grammar, syntax, and semantics. The course will give benefits to the students in gaining skills in critical analysis, writing and reasoning. History of the Emergence of Bangladesh Course Code: BDS 1201 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Description The course has been designed to facilitate the students in obtaining the inclusive idea about struggling past, diverse culture and heritage of Bangladesh in the light of long historical background. It will focus on the social, economic and political developments that have taken place before and since its independence in the 20th century. Fundamentals of Mathematics Course Code: MATH 1105 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course objectives: This course intends to build students strengths to increase overall mathematical understanding and skill. Students will get an intense foundational introduction to the fundamental concepts in Mathematics. This course will train students on several topics including mathematical relevance; linear relationships; exponents and polynomials; rational expressions and equations; exponential and logarithmic functions; and geometry and calculus. Biophysical Chemistry Course Code: CHEM 1103 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: The course content is designed to make students understand and identify the thermodynamic systems and processes, understand the basic principles of thermodynamics and electrochemistry, and know how to apply them to explain and interpret the observations in other areas of chemistry and related fields. Bioorganic Chemistry Course Code: CHEM 2103 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: In this course the basics in bioorganic chemistry and its inception will be focused. The course will enable students to understand the concepts of organic chemistry and provide opportunities to learn about the applications of the laws of chemistry in biological processes. Physics for Biologists-I Course Code: PHY 1201 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course is designed to enable students to know the basic principles behind all physics that can be applied in biology. Enable students to learn the use of biological examples of physical principles. Physics for Biologists-II Course Code: PHY 2101 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course introduces the use of physical methods in the study of biological systems. This course will introduce students about electromagnetic (EM) waves and its applications. Also, will focus on imaging and related systems. Basics of Computing and Information Technology Course Code: CSE 2001 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: The objective of this course is to provide computation and IT knowledge to get trained manpower for using computers as well as write the software required for the effective and efficient use of the computers and IT. This course will help to prepare students with broad, integrated knowledge in basic computer and IT including communications, computer networking, computer-based systems, database management, website development, digital media and electronic publishing etc. Software fundamentals in Computation Course Code: CSE 3001 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Introduction to the Course: The course introduces computer programming and software development. It benefits individuals pursuing programming and software development as well as anyone in the IT field who works with programmers and systems analysts. The course also covers programming concepts common to modern languages, including C, C, Java, etc. Biostatistics Course Code: MATH 3101 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course is designed to provide a broad overview of biostatistics methods as well as applications commonly used for research. This course enables students to learn about statistical data, data collection parameters and understand the methods for analyzing data. The students will also learn how to differentiate significant data by statistical tests. Core Courses on Biotechnology and Genetic Engineering (BGE): General Biology Course Code: BGE 1001 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: The objective of the course is to introduce student with basic biology. The course will enable students to gain basic knowledge on origin of life; ecology; biodiversity; nature of microbes, protista, plants and animals, and their reproductive strategies. Basic Biochemistry Course Code: BGE 1002 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course objectives: The objective of this course is to enable students to understand the structure and functions of cells, their organization and processes at molecular level. Students will understand the structures and physico-chemical properties of biomolecules such as sugars, amino acids, and nucleic acids. Introductory Biotechnology and Genetic Engineering Course Code: BGE 1003 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course will enable students to recognize the basic concepts of traditional and modern biotechnology. Students will be able to broaden their knowledge on wide applications of biotechnology in various fields. This course will also enable students to know the basic tools used in genetic engineering technology. Basic Microbiology Course Code: BGE 1004 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: Basic Microbiology is a fundamental course to let the students know about the nature and diversity of microorganisms and their potential implications. The course will cover comparative properties of prokaryotic microbes, as well as their classification, identifications, reproduction, and their roles as disease causing agents. This course will also focus on the basic principles of microscopy and their applications. Enzymes and Enzyme Kinetics Course Code: BGE 2001 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course is designed to let the students know various theoretical and practical aspects of enzymology. The study of this course will enable students to learn the structure, function, and kinetics of enzymes. Basics of Molecular Biology Course Code: BGE 2002 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: The objective of this course is to enable the students to know the chemical and functional aspects of the genetic material of the organisms. The course will also elaborate on the molecular mechanisms of DNA replication, transcription, protein synthesis, and gene regulation. Protein Structure and Function Course Code: BGE 2003 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course covers structural and functional features of proteins. This enables students to understand primary, secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structure in proteins and identify the types of interactions important in each case. Molecular Genetics Course Code: BGE 2004 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course is designed to let the students know about the organization of genome structure and the central role of genome in controlling cellular behavior. This course will also enable students to learn about epigenetic modifications and their function in regulating gene expression. Bioenergetics and Metabolism Course Code: BGE 2005 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course is designed with an aim to let the students know about the importance of energy flow through living systems. This course describes different cellular processes such as cellular respiration and other metabolic processes that lead to production and utilization of energy. Cell Biology Course Code: BGE 2006 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course covers the knowledge about the molecular and cell-based functions of life focusing on mechanisms that facilitate development of multicellular organisms. This course will also provide knowledge about cellular organelles, their functions and cell division. Human Physiology Course Code: BGE 2007 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course is designed to enable the students to learn anatomical structure and functions of various body systems. The students also learn how cells, tissues, organs, and systems function together to maintain organisms life. Animal and Plant Tissue Culture Course Code: BGE 3001 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: The objective of this course is to let the students know how the animal and plant cells are cultured and maintained. Media requirements, supporting instruments, aseptic conditions, cryopreservation and recovery, and assessment of cell growthhealth are also focused. Basic Immunology Course Code: BGE 3002 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course is designed to let the students understand mammalian immune response and identify components of innate and adaptive immune systems. This course helps to familiarize the students with the different types of immunoglobulins and their functions. Students also learn about antigen-antibody interaction and antigen presentation. Genomics, Proteomic and Bioinformatics Course Code: BGE 3003 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course is designed to introduce the students about genomes, proteomes and databases that store various data about genes and proteins. This course explains the application of computational methods to address problems in molecular biology. This is an important course in modern biology, and the goal is to familiarize students with biological data and software. Agriculture Biotechnology Course Code: BGE 3004 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: The objective of this course is to give an understanding of the advanced biotechnological concepts for agricultural products particularly crops improvement. The course will emphasize the selective techniques used for plant cells and organs culture, micropropagation, genetic engineering of crop plants and its application etc. Animal Biotechnology Course Code: BGE 3005 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: The objective of the course is to conceptualize specific knowledge about animal biotechnology. The course will provide students an opportunity to come across various scientific techniques for understanding of different aspect of animal biotechnology. Molecular Biology of the Diseases Course Code: BGE 3006 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course enables students to recognize the basic concepts of disease mechanisms. Students are equipped with an understanding of recent advances in diagnosis and treatment of diseases at the molecular level. The course also provides opportunities to identify the contributing risk factors and the changing profile of different disease incidences worldwide. Recombinant DNA Technology Course Code: BGE 3007 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course conceptualizes basic knowledge about Recombinant DNA Technology. It helps to acquire technique-oriented knowledge on different areas of recombinant DNA technology especially restriction modification system, generating cloning vector and gene library, transformation and efficient expression of gene etc. Microbial Genetics Course Code: BGE 3008 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: The objective of this course is to allow students to understand the mechanism of gene regulation in prokaryotes and to broaden the horizon of knowledge related to prokaryotic molecular biology. It also creates opportunities to learn basic concepts of rDNA technology implemented in microbial world. Developmental Biology Course Code: BGE 3009 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Introduction to the Course: This course is designed to provide the fundamental concepts of cellular, molecular and genetic aspects of developmental biology. This helps students to gain underlying principles of developmental strategies from fertilized egg to adult animals especially in model organisms. The study of this course makes students understand the significance of gene regulatory proteins and signalling molecules in embryonic stages. Fermentation Technology and Bioprocessing Course Code: BGE 4001 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course emphasizes the application of biological and engineering principles to problems involving microbial, mammalian, and biologicalbiochemical systems. This course helps to develop better understanding about operations and commercial opportunities in fermentation-based biotechnology. Students get an opportunity to develop knowledge on a variety of fermentation strategies. Biotechnology of Microbial System Course Code: BGE 4002 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course is designed to give a view about the potential of microbes for producing various industrially important products. The students will get in touch with various applications and ways of microbial gene manipulation for the production of economically important products and processes. Computational Genomics and System Biology Course Code: BGE 4003 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course is designed to provide students the background and recent advancements in computational and systems biology. It eemphasizes getting deeper insights into the fundamentals of molecular network biology. Tools and techniques in mathematical modeling of the biological processes are also introduced. Medical Biotechnology Course Code: BGE 4004 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course covers different prospects and applications of medical biotechnology. It provides an in-depth understanding of the health-related core principles and methodologies. Students acquire a broad grounding in genetic diseases, with the emphasis on the molecular aspects of disease diagnosis and pharmacogenomics, particularly in relation to human disease. Cellular Communication and Signaling Course Code: BGE 4005 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course provides an overview of the cellar signal transduction mechanism. Students are introduced to signaling moleculesreceptors and the general principles of cell signaling. Various signaling pathways involving G-protein coupled receptors; enzyme coupled receptors; signaling in plantsmicroorganisms and regulation of signaling pathways are discussed. GMOs, Biosafety and Bioethics Course Code: BGE 4006 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course conceptualizes general knowledge on biosafety, biosecurity and bioethics. Also describes general techniques used in biosafety and bioethics. Thee students supposed to understand and follow the regulatory framework important for the product safety and benefit for the society. At the end of the course, it is expected that students have understood the basic issues of biosafety and bioethics and is expected that they will be more confidant to practice and implement all these policies in their future endeavor. Advanced Molecular Biology Course Code: BGE 4008 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course is designed to teach the students about the evolution of genome and integrate the perspectives of genomic inheritance and regulation, the central role of genome in controlling cellular behavior. Moreover, the course will help in gaining perspective on processes complementary to the genetic information of life. This course broadens the horizon of knowledge related to advanced molecular biology. Virology and Oncology Course Code: BGE 4009 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: The purpose of this course is to provide knowledge in the general field of molecular virology with an emphasis on the molecular biology of tumor viruses and oncogenes. The course encompasses elaboration on viruses that infects organisms of all domains of life. The also contain description on general mechanism of cancer occurrence, its diagnostics and treatment options. Methods in Biotechnology Course Code: BGE 4010 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: The course covers state of the art techniques and methods in molecular biotechnology. The students gain an understanding of the practical use and theory behind the newest techniques within the field of biotechnology and become capable to employ gained knowledge to solve problems. Environmental Biotechnology Course Code: BGE 4011 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course is designed to help students understand the importance of environmental biotechnology. The course focuses on the utilization of microbial processes in waste and water treatment, and bioremediation. It also enables students to come up with ideas that can help preventing the environment pollution. Aquaculture and Marine Biotechnology Course Code: BGE 4012 Credit Hour: 3 Prerequisite: Course Objectives: This course is designed to let the students know how to develop useful products and process from the marine resources. It is also for aquaculture production and productivity increase through improved technology with the adoption of biotechnology tools and techniques. The knowledge from this course is expected to provide benefit to the aquatic and marine sectors and help scientific research on various sectors of Aquaculture  Marine Biotechnology addressing areas such as feed and nutrition, health, environment, and productivity increase. title: Curriculum Structure - UIU - Department of Biotechnology and Genetic Engineering
content: Curriculum Structure UG ProgramAdmission Requirements Course Plan Curriculum Structure Program Requirement Degree Requirements The degree of B.Sc. in Biotechnology and Genetic Engineering will be conferred by the University when a student will satisfactorily complete all the required courses offered to himher over a period of 4 (four) academic years. Each academic year is divided into two semesters. Duration of Semesters: The duration of a semester is 6 (six) months including Class Tests, Assignments, Mid-term and Final Examination. The duration of a semester is 20 (twenty) weeks which may be used as follows: Classes (Theoretical and Practical) 7 weeks Mid-Term Examination 3 weeks Classes (Theoretical and Practical) 7 weeks Final Examination 3 weeks Total 20 weeks Grading System: The total performance of a student in a given course is based on a scheme of continuous assessment. For theoretical courses this continuous assessment is made through homework, assignment, attendance, quizzes, etc. The distribution of marks for a given course will be as follows: I. Class Attendance 5 II. Class Tests 20 III. Assignments 5 IV. Mid-Term Exam 30 V. Final Exam 40 Total: 100 The assessment in laboratory courses will be made through observation of the student at work in class, viva voce during laboratory hours and quizzes. Minimum Attendance in the Class will be 80 as per existing UIU policy. Each course has a number of credits, which describes its corresponding weights. A letter grade with a specific number of grade points is awarded to each course for which a student is registered. A student has to earn a minimum CGPA (Cumulative Grade Point Average) of 2.0 to qualify for the next semester. A student will be on probation if heshe earns a minimum CGPA of less than 2.0. title: Admission Requirements - UIU - Department of Biotechnology and Genetic Engineering
content: Admission Requirements UG ProgramAdmission Requirements Course Plan Curriculum Structure Program Requirement Degree Requirements Every applicant, without any exception, must fulfil the admission requirements as laid down by the University. Admission Test and Interview for admission into a semester will be held as decided by the University and the department of Biotechnology and Genetic Engineering. A Higher Secondary Certificate or its equivalent in Science with Mathematics, Biology and Chemistry or other fields of study are the basic educational requirements to get admission to this program. Entry Requirements: Following entry requirements will be considered for the students seeking admission to Bachelor of Science in Biotechnology and Genetic Engineering (BGE) Program under the School of Life Science (SoLS). A minimum GPA of 2.52nd divisionequivalent grade in SSC and HSC or equivalent public examinations. Students with GPA 2.00 in any examination either SSC or HSC, however, must have a minimum GPA of 6.00 totalling the GPA of both the examinations. O-level students must have completed a minimum of 5 subjects with Average Grade Point of 2.50 or above and A-level students a minimum of 2 subjects with Average Grade Point of 2.00 or above (scale A5, B4, C3, D2, E1) The students, who are children of freedom fighters, will be eligible for getting admission if they have a minimum GPA of 5.00 totalling the GPA of SSC and HSC Examinations. Such students, however, have to submit the copy of authenticated documents as the proof of hisher fathermothers identity as a freedom fighter. Acceptable score in UIU Admission Test. Admission Test is not required for GPA 5.00 holders in H.S.Cequivalent level of exams and credit transferred students for getting admission to an undergraduate program. GED result will not be accepted. Admission Test Applicants will be required to sit for an Admission Test designed to judge their abilities and aptitude for the program. The Test will be held as arranged by the University and department. The Admission Test will be held on the following three areas: Language and Communication Biology Chemistry To qualify in a Written Test, an applicant is required to obtain a minimum mark in all the three sections separately.

And to last in the competition to grab opportunity the classroom based education is not enough. Therefore, it is necessary to open more learning process to develop students mental faculty, intellectual ability and inner qualities. This learning process can bring benefit when a student side by side with his academic curriculum participates in co-curricular activities i.e. debate, seminar, symposium, workshop, cultural program, community services program and games and sports of his own choice and likings. With this aim in view, co-curricular activities of our university have been evaluated and accordingly the Directorate of Student Affairs has been set up which plays the central role in the development and growth of students in co-curricular activities. These student activities are promoted through a number of student clubs. The clubs are UIU Debate Club (UIUDC), UIU Cultural Club (UIUCC), UIU Theater  Film Club (UIUTFC), UIU Business Club (UIUBC), UIU Computer Club (UIUCCL), UIU Electrical  Electronic Club (UIUEEC), UIU Photography Club (UIUPC), UIU Social Services Club (UIUSSC), UIU Sports Club (UIUSC), UIU MBA Club (UIUMC) The clubs are having student committees administered by the Moderator (Faculty Member).The club activities are coordinated by the Directorate of Student Affairs (DSA) headed by the Director of Student Affairs assisted by the Executive  Asst. Director of DSA. The Directorate provides all sorts of support services to the student clubs. The clubs are engaged in continuous innovation and intellectual creativity. One of the major Services of Directorate of Student Affairs (DSA) Office for creating the opportunities of co-curricular and extracurricular activities for the student is to nurture a several number of clubs to explore and support the talents of students. DSA also arranges interest free loan for the Students in the emergency and urgent need of them. Since last one year, UIU DSA office has disbursed at least 30 lacs taka as interest free loan among the UIU students. In addition to that, UIU and United Group provide donation or financial support from UIU Welfare Fund to the Students who suffer from the sudden crisis happening during the Study life at UIU. Recreational Facilities UIU provides round  the-year indoor and outdoor recreational facilities.UIU indoor sports center is located at the main campus.UIU clubs organize indoor and outdoor games, debates, seminars, workshops, cultural programs, educational tours and also participate in different inter university tournaments.UIU students also participate in voluntary blood donation program, community and humanitarian services program Some clubs publish newsletters, magazines etc. There is a separate common room for the female students with light equipments for physical exercise. UIU Gymnasium is well-equipped and it is run by Asst. Director, Physical Education (Professional Instructor) to train the Gym enthusiasts. Internship Placement Internships are arranged with top organizations and financial institutions for the students to get an exposure to professional life in their respective field of study. Job Placement and Job Search Career Counseling Center assists students search and find suitable part-time jobs. Arranges full time placements either immediately after graduation or over a period of time. Besides, the placement function Career Counseling Center is also involved in arranging workshops and seminars to practice on resume writing, interview techniques, job search skills and presentation techniques. Alumni Association It is the expectation of the authorities of UIU that one day the graduates and the former students will be creating opportunities for the current students. Career Counseling Center has started to work on creating a database of the ex-students, where they are placed etc. Students should send their CVs along with a scanned copy of photograph to the email address : careeruiu.ac.bd and submit the hard copy of the same to the Career Counseling Center for Internship or Job Placement. title: Dr. Ohidujjaman - UIU - Department of CSE
content: Dr. Ohidujjaman Assistant Professor, Dept. of CSE ROOM: 335 (1-3) C PABX: 3308 Email: ohidujjamancse.uiu.ac.bd Profile Scopus: https:www.scopus.comauthiddetail.uri?authorId57136845100 Web of Science: https:www.webofscience.comwosauthorrecordKIG-4207-2024 Google Scholar: https:scholar.google.comcitations?user6b3nDr8AAAAJhlen ORCID: https:orcid.org0000-0002-8776-7145 Contact: ohidujjamancse.uiu.ac.bd; tuhin.iu31gmail.com; tuhin_iu31yahoo.com Biography: Dr. Ohidujjaman received his B.Sc. (Honors) and M.Sc. degrees in Computer Science  Engineering from Islamic University, Kushtia, and United International University, Dhaka, Bangladesh, in 2008 and 2014, respectively. He obtained his PhD degree in Science and Engineering from the Graduate School of Science  Engineering at Saitama University, Saitama, Japan, in 2024. He is awarded the scholastic honor ICT Scholarship at B.Sc. and Summa Cum Laude at M.Sc. in 2005 and 2014, respectively. He worked as a Research Assistant at the Graduate School of Science  Engineering, Saitama University, Japan, from September 2022 to March 2024. Dr. Ohidujjaman is a former faculty member of Daffodil International University, Hamdard University Bangladesh, and Dhaka International University, respectively. content: Mr. Mohammad Mamun Elahi Assistant Professor, Dept. of CSE ROOM: 518 PABX: 1401 Email: mmelahicse.uiu.ac.bd Bio Mohammad Mamun Elahi has obtained his B.Sc. in CSE from BUET in 1997 and joined the University of Asia Pacific as a Lecturer in 1997. He completed his M.Sc. in Computer Science from Wright State University, Ohio, USA and joined UIU as an Assistant Professor in 2005. He is currently pursuing his PhD in the field of Edge-enabled Vehicular Networks at Military Institute of Science  Technology (MIST). Since the launching of Cisco Networking Academy at UIU in 2007 till date, he has been serving as the Legal Main Contact (LMC) and Curriculum Head of the academy. He is also working as the founder and director of Center for Emerging Networks and Technologies Research (CENTeR) established on June 2019 at UIU. Besides teaching, he had worked as local consultant in a number of projects and was involved in database designing, software development, and deployment. Some of the projects are National Water Resources Database (NWRD), Arsenic Decision Support System (ADSS), Soil and Land Resource Information System (SOLARIS) under Center for Environmental and Geographic Information System (CEGIS). He has also worked as a Technical Expert in FBCCI web portal development. title: Recent Success story of CSE Students’ – “Clean Dhaka” - UIU - Department of CSE
content: News Recent Success story of CSE Students  Clean Dhaka December 15, 2019 SHARE: Clean Dhaka- a Team of UIU Robotics comprising students of Dept. of CSE, recently secured winning positions at two Business Idea Competitions (ENTREPRENEURSHIP 360  Hult Prize Challenge UIU). ENTREPRENEURSHIP 360: FNF Bangladesh  Dnet Presented ENTREPRENEURSHIP 360 (ROAD TO HACKATHON) was organized by UIU Entrepreneur Development Forum  UIUEDF  UIU CCC. It was a two day (18 hours) Hackathon that ran from 28 October 2019 to 29 October 2019 (Monday-Tuesday). The goal of this Hackathon was to provide supplemental knowledge on social, psychological and cultural perspectives including business management and sustainability, for creating successful entrepreneurs by transforming their innovation into a successful business. Clean Dhaka secured the 1st Runner UP position at this Hackathon. Teams from both BBA  CSE participated in this event. Hult Prize Challenge UIU: The Hult Prize was established by Bertil Hult and is an annual, year-long competition that crowd-sources ideas from MBA and college students after challenging them to solve a pressing social issue around topics such as food security, water access, energy, and education. UIU Junior Economists Forum, a wing of UIU Career Counseling Center, arranged the on-campus round of the worlds largest startup competition. The Mission of Hult Prize 2020 is to solve real-life problems and make revenue from it at the same time. 50 teams participated in this competition and among them, 12 teams were selected for the semi-final round. Team Clean Dhaka from UIU Robotics made way for the Grand Finale by going through an analytical Idea Presentation procedure. The team became 2nd Runners Up out of the top 6 finalist teams by giving a final pitch in front of a Judge Panel consisting of renowned experts in both the Business and Tech industries of Bangladesh. title: Seminar on “Shaping Your Future in the Global Semiconductor Industry with ULKASEMI” Successfully Held at UIU - UIU - Department of EEE
content: News Seminar on Shaping Your Future in the Global Semiconductor Industry with ULKASEMI Successfully Held at UIU September 10, 2025 SHARE: The IEEE UIU Student Branch, in collaboration with the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE), successfully organized a seminar titled Shaping Your Future in the Global Semiconductor Industry with ULKASEMI on Tuesday, 26th August 2025, at the Innovation Hub (10th Floor), United International University (UIU). The seminar featured Bangladeshs largest semiconductor company, ULKASEMI, which provided students with invaluable insights into the rapidly growing global semiconductor industry. The session was specifically designed for students of EEE and CSE, aiming to bridge the gap between academic knowledge and real-world industry practices. Distinguished Speakers The seminar was graced by two prominent professionals from ULKASEMI: Moon Sadia Dipthee, Director, Analog Layout Design Md. Muzammel Hossain, Senior Manager, Branding  PR Both speakers shared their expertise and experiences, highlighting the opportunities and challenges of the semiconductor sector. They emphasized the importance of skill development, innovation, and global perspectives for young engineers aspiring to build successful careers in this field. Key Discussions and Takeaways The current trends and future prospects of the semiconductor industry worldwide Possible career pathways for Bangladeshi graduates in EEE and CSE The role of research, innovation, and technical skills in shaping future opportunities An interactive QA session, where students directly engaged with industry leaders The program witnessed an active participation of UIU students, who expressed their enthusiasm and gained practical knowledge beyond their academic curriculum. The Department of EEE extends its appreciation to ULKASEMI for collaborating in this significant initiative and congratulates IEEE UIU Student Branch for organizing a successful and impactful seminar that will inspire students to envision their future in the global semiconductor industry. title: UIU EEC Successfully Conducts Workshop on Transformer Design - UIU - Department of EEE
content: News UIU EEC Successfully Conducts Workshop on Transformer Design August 20, 2025 SHARE: On August 9, 2025 the UIU Electrical  Electronic Club (UIU EEC) organized a highly informative workshop on Transformer Design, delivered by Dr. Intekab Alam, Professor of the Department of EEE. The event provided students with a valuable mix of theoretical foundations and practical, hands-on learning. The session introduced participants to core principles of transformer design and operation, and complemented the theory with real materials, essential components, and demonstrations using small transformers. This practical approach helped students visualize the design process and clarified several complex concepts. Attendees benefited from step-by-step explanations and live demonstrations that linked classroom theory to real engineering practice. The hands-on exposure not only reinforced technical understanding but also encouraged students to think creatively about future applications in electrical engineering. The workshop served as an effective platform for knowledge sharing and skill building, fostering both technical competence and curiosity among participants. Students left the session better equipped to approach transformer-related projects and research with confidence. title: EEE Project Show — Spring 2025 - UIU - Department of EEE
content: News EEE Project Show  Spring 2025 August 20, 2025 SHARE: On 4 August 2025, the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE) at United International University, supported by the UIU Electrical  Electronic Club (UIUEEC), successfully hosted the EEE Project Show  Spring 2025 at the UIU campus in Dhaka. The one-day exhibition provided a professional platform for undergraduate students to present their semester-long projects, demonstrating practical skills, engineering rigor, and creative problem-solving across hardware and software domains. The event featured three competitive categories  Software Group, Senior Group, and Junior Group  enabling a broad representation of topics including embedded systems, power electronics, IoT and remote monitoring, robotics and control, AIML applications, and software simulation tools. Teams presented working prototypes or live demonstrations alongside concise technical documentation, and engaged with a panel of faculty judges during question-and-answer sessions. Students displayed strong competence in translating theoretical knowledge into real-world solutions: many projects included clear problem statements, well-defined objectives, test plans, and measured performance results. Presentations emphasized not only technical design but also usability, safety, cost considerations, and potential for further development or deployment. A distinguished faculty panel assessed each entry using a transparent rubric that rewarded innovation, technical depth, demonstration quality, documentation, and presentation skills. UIUEEC volunteers handled logistics, registration, and on-site coordination, ensuring smooth setup and timekeeping. The result was a professionally run showcase that celebrated student initiative, fostered peer learning, and highlighted the EEE departments commitment to hands-on, application-driven engineering education. title: Seminar on “Renewable Resource Assessment Using GIS: Estimating Solar PV Potential in Bangladesh” Held at UIU - UIU - Department of EEE
content: News Seminar on Renewable Resource Assessment Using GIS: Estimating Solar PV Potential in Bangladesh Held at UIU August 20, 2025 SHARE: On 13 August 2025, the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE) of United International University (UIU)  the Centre for Energy Research (CER) , in collaboration with the UIU Electrical and Electronic Club (UIUEEC), successfully organized an informative seminar titled Renewable Resource Assessment Using GIS: Estimating Solar PV Potential in Bangladesh. The session was conducted by Dr. Mominul Hasan, one of UIU EEEs proud alumni, who brings extensive expertise in solar PV, energy system modelling, and community-engaged learning. His recent PhD research explored unlocking Bangladeshs solar PV deployment potential through policy and technological innovation Dr. Mominul Hasan also shared his extensive expertise in the field of renewable energy and geographic information system (GIS) applications. Dr. Hasan elaborated on how GIS-based approaches can accurately assess solar photovoltaic (PV) potential in different regions of Bangladesh, enabling policymakers, researchers, and investors to make data-driven decisions for sustainable energy development. A highlight of the seminar was Dr. Hasans discussion on Germanys renewable energy journey, where he presented comparative insights into the German approach to solar energy integration. This segment provided attendees with a global perspective, showcasing successful policy frameworks, technological innovations, and implementation strategies that Bangladesh could adopt to accelerate its renewable energy transition. Also present at the event were Dr. Kaled Masukur Rahman, Professor and Head of the Department of EEE, and Mr. Md. Shahriar Ahmed Chowdhury, Assistant Professor of EEE and Director of CER. Both shared inspiring remarks, encouraging students to actively engage in research and innovation in renewable energy to contribute to a sustainable future for Bangladesh. The interactive session allowed participants to engage directly with the speaker, asking questions related to both local and international renewable energy practices. Students, faculty members, and renewable energy enthusiasts attended the seminar, gaining valuable academic and practical knowledge. The event concluded with a note of appreciation to Dr. Mominul Hasan for his enlightening presentation and to all participants for their active involvement. The seminar reaffirmed UIUs commitment to fostering awareness, research, and innovation in the field of renewable energy, paving the way for a greener, cleaner future. title: IEEE UIU SB Industry Visit to Augmedix Bangladesh - UIU - Department of EEE
content: News IEEE UIU SB Industry Visit to Augmedix Bangladesh August 17, 2025 SHARE: Exploring Silicon Valley Innovation from Dhaka On August 14, 2025, a group of 25 enthusiastic students from the Departments of Electrical  Electronic Engineering (EEE) at United International University (UIU) participated in an enriching industry visit to Augmedix Bangladesh  a Silicon Valley-based healthtech company that operates in the USA, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka. Augmedix is widely known for its real-time medical documentation services, combining the power of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with remote medical scribes to support doctors and healthcare professionals globally. Their solutions are now used in more than 100 clinics and hospitals across the United States, making significant contributions to the digital healthcare ecosystem. The session began with a warm welcome from Mr. Rashed Noman, Country Director of Augmedix Bangladesh. He shared the inspiring journey of how Augmedix transformed from a startup into a globally recognized company that now provides thousands of jobs while revolutionizing healthcare documentation around the world. His motivational speech encouraged students to think innovatively and work towards global standards. Following the introductory session, students had an insightful interaction with the Augmedix technical team. The engineers demonstrated how their AI-driven software platform operates in real-time to assist physicians during patient consultations. The technical team presented key tools and workflows that ensure efficiency and accuracy in clinical documentation. Students had the opportunity to explore: How remote medical scribes work in real-time with doctors in the US The integration of AI for speech-to-text conversion and electronic health records Augmedixs internal work culture and operational processes The broader impact of AI in the future of global healthcare As a gesture of appreciation, a token of thanks was handed over to Augmedix Bangladesh by Naimul Haque, Chairperson of IEEE UIU Student Branch. This moment symbolized the strong connection between academia and industry, and UIU commitment to building bridges with leading technology companies. This industry tour to Augmedix Bangladesh was not just an educational outing  it was a doorway to understanding how technological innovation can create meaningful global impact. The IEEE UIU Student Branch continues to take such initiatives to expose UIU students to real-world industry environments, helping them become future-ready engineers. The laboratory work provides the student with experience of power system model computation and analysis through application of different software (Multisim, MATLAB, Simulink, ETAP) and exposure to modeling and analysis of different power system components and the measurement of its different parameters. This course is a continuation of EEE-3205 (Power system), which provides students with a working knowledge of power system problems and computer techniques used to solve some of these problems. Topics include: determining line parameters, load flow analysis, fault study, designing PLC based simple protective relaying system etc. Major experiments: 1: Study of Electrical Grid Network Power system of Bangladesh- recent scenario.2. Measurement of Negative and Zero sequence impedance of an unloaded synchronous generator.3. Determination of BUS admittance matrix and finding BUS voltages using Gauss-Seidal Power flow solution method.4. Determination of transmission line parameters.5. Designing simple protective relaying system using Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) and IDMT overcurrent relay.6. Study of symmetrical and unsymmetrical faults in a power network using Simulink and ETAP. Major components: CTPT PLCFrequency Drive Synchronous Machine Relay Three-phase Transformer  Software used: Electronic Workbench PSpice MatlabSimulink

It offers a broad range of services, including book circulation, reference assistance, research counseling, bibliographic documentation, and retrospective searches. The librarys collection includes a balanced mix of books, journals, and various media formats, reflecting a wide range of subjects such as arts, business, engineering, sciences, and professional programs. With a vast collection exceeding 25,000 items, the library houses books, CDsDVDs, journals, magazines, and newspapers. UIU library subscribe e-journal from JSTOR, with comprising 2,895 journal titles. And a single e-book database, Wiley, with includes 3,500 titles. Major Services provided by the UIU library Circulation Service Clearance Service E-Resource Service Audio-Visual Service Periodical  Newspaper Service Internet Access Reference Assistance Browsing facilities The library is equipped with 41 browsing computers, all offering high-speed internet access. Users can browse and download materials from these computers or use their own laptops within the library. Koha Intergraded Library software The UIU Library uses KOHA, a comprehensive library management system. KOHA automates key functions such as book check-ins and check-outs, allowing users to search for books and monitor their borrowing history and status.
